title: Communication failure in Omnipod Dash
symptom: Users of the Blackview n6000 device report an error every few hours that AAPS does not find the pod, the official bluetooth app crashes until the device crashes and restarts. The only solution found is to turn off bluetooth until AAPS direct protocol finds the pump with bluetooth off, then turn it back on so Dexcom continues to work. Some users experience no communication with the pod for several hours, and sometimes the Google Play Service application crashes.
cause: The thread does not establish a definitive root cause. There is speculation about a conflict with the Diakem app (Dexcom G7 app) and possible Bluetooth instability on the Blackview n6000, but no confirmed cause.
fix: No definitive fix is stated. Workarounds mentioned include turning Bluetooth off and on again, uninstalling the DASH app, or shutting down the Diakem app to re-establish connection. However, these are not universally effective, and the maintainer suggests changing the phone if connection is unreliable.
evidence_quote: I believe there is nothing we can do on AAPS side. Change your phone if the connection is not reliable
